title: Extract read-optimized tenant projections and compact join paths
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Reduce high-latency, join-heavy control-plane read paths by creating compact, read-optimized tenant projections that eliminate expensive multi-table joins for common API and console queries.
description:
Problem: A set of frontend and control-plane APIs (tenant dashboard, rollout list, project quotas, and recent-events feeds) rely on wide, high-cardinality joins across events, projects, tenants, and audit tables. These queries cause frequent planner misestimates, repeated index scans, and volatile p99 latencies during bursty workloads. The current hot path includes joining a large events_payload JSONB column and multiple polymorphic references which inflates row width and prevents compact indexes.

Goals: 1) Reduce median and p95/p99 control-plane read latency for dashboard and read-only APIs by introducing denormalized, read-optimized projections. 2) Lower CPU and I/O on primary control-plane DB during peak syncs by avoiding repeated multi-table joins. 3) Provide an online, reversible migration with feature-flagged rollout and data validation checks.

Constraints: must be compatible with Dedicated and Private control plane deployments (no breaking changes to replication/CDC contracts). Backfill must run without causing write amplification or long-lasting locks on production tables.
proposed_solution:
Create a small set of tenant_projections tables that denormalize the most common read fields (tenant_id, project_id, active_rollout_count, last_event_ts, quota_used, flags_summary). Implement the projections as: 1) a lightweight materialized view maintained by periodic incremental refresh for lower-volume fields and 2) a trigger-backed incremental update path for high-velocity counters where near-real-time is required. Replace the heaviest reads in the API/console to query the projection table instead of performing multi-join plans that include large JSONB columns.

Additional optimization: move the large events_payload JSONB out of the hot join path into events_payload_blob (separate table keyed by event_id) so common list queries can avoid loading payloads. Add compact composite partial indexes tuned to the projection filters (tenant_id, status, last_event_ts) and a small hash column for polymorphic ref resolution to avoid wide FK joins.

Rationale: this hybrid approach balances write cost (triggers add small per-row overhead) versus read benefits (orders-of-magnitude fewer index lookups and no repeated JSONB scans). Materialized-view refresh windows and trigger paths are controllable by feature flags to tune trade-offs per deployment tier.
migration_plan: 1) Schema: create tenant_projections and events_payload_blob tables with appropriate constraints (no exclusive locks). 2) Backfill: run parallel chunked COPY jobs from a consistent snapshot; use batching (500-2k rows/chunk) and parallel workers to keep wall time < 3 hours for largest tenants. 3) Validation: run row counts and checksum diffs between queries against canonical joins and the projection results for a sample of tenants. 4) Switch reads: behind a feature flag, route console and API reads to projection tables for a staged subset (internal -> beta customers -> all). 5) Monitor: validate error rates, staleness (max allowed ms), and key metrics (p95/p99 latency, DB CPU, IO) for 7 days per stage. 6) Cleanup: once stable and backfill complete, stop maintaining the materialized view refresh job for fields migrated to triggers and mark old join-heavy queries as deprecated for removal in a follow-up ticket.
rollback_plan: If regressions are detected (increased error rate, data drift above thresholds, or unexpected resource usage), flip the feature flag to route reads back to canonical join queries. For partial backfills, mark incomplete tenants as routed to old path until backfill finishes. If trigger overhead causes write latency regressions, pause triggers by switching projection maintenance to periodic batch refresh and investigate incremental trigger throttling. All schema additions are additive; in worst case we keep the projections disabled and drop the new background workers.
testing_plan: Unit tests for projection population logic and trigger handlers. Integration: end-to-end staging run with synthetic load (mix of read-heavy dashboard traffic and write bursts). Load test: simulate 3x peak traffic and measure p95/p99 latency and DB CPU with and without projection reads. Data validation: nightly checksum job and a diff harness that samples tenant ids to compare canonical join result vs projection result. Observability: new Grafana panels for projection hit-rate, staleness distribution, backfill progress, and trigger lag; alerts on >1% mismatch or staleness >5s for trigger-backed fields.
acceptance_criteria: Console tenant list p95 latency reduced by >=50% compared to baseline
No data mismatches in the sampled checksum diff (0 drift) after backfill
Backfill completes for all tenants within the maintenance window and without causing replication lag > 60s
Feature-flag rollout to 100% with stable error rate and no increased write latency
Partial indexes on projection columns reduce index-only scans for top queries (validated via EXPLAIN ANALYZE)
progress_updates: 2026-02-01: Design reviewed with platform and infra; agreed on hybrid trigger+materialized approach. Action: Arjun to prototype trigger handler and Maya to draft backfill plan.
2026-02-15: Prototype completed on staging; projection read path shows 3x lower p95 in synthetic test. Observed 4% write overhead with trigger-backed counters; acceptable for dedicated tiers.

2026-02-28: Backfill tooling (chunked parallel copy) implemented; initial dry-run on a medium-sized tenant completed in 22 minutes. Minor checksum mismatch discovered (timestamp rounding) and patched in hygiene step.
2026-03-05: Feature flag infra added to API gateway and console. Starting canary (internal team) to validate correctness and monitoring hooks.
2026-03-10: Canary stable for 48h; p95 improved 58%, DB CPU down 27% during read bursts. Planning staged rollout to beta customers next week.
Next steps: Schedule full backfill weekend, coordinate on-call rotation, and finalize rollout cutoff metrics.
notes: Avoid wide FK cascades during backfill; use referenced ids instead of joining to heavy lookup tables. For Private deployments where CDC/replication rules differ, provide an opt-out flag to disable triggers and rely on scheduled refreshes. Follow-up tickets should remove deprecated join query paths and add long-term compaction of events_payload_blob using per-tenant TTL policies.
